properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 29 at 5:51PM MDT until July 29 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 550 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 14 miles southwest
of Florence, or 37 miles west of Pueblo, moving southeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of south
central Fremont and north central Custer Counties.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 5:47PM MDT until July 29 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Gold Mountain Burn Area in...
Southeastern Ouray County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 547 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Gold Mountain Burn Area. Between 0.8 and 1.3
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is already occurring.

Excessive rainfall over the warning area will cause mud slides near
steep terrain. The mud slide can consist of rock, mud, vegetation
and other loose materials.

This is a FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for Cutler and Dexter Creek. This
is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Gold
Mountain Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK
HIGHER GROUND NOW! IMMEDIATE EVACUATION for areas in
and around the Gold Mountain Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ouray.

Areas along Highway 550, County Roads 23 and 17 between Dexter and
Cutler Creek.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 5:47PM MDT until July 29 at 8:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The North and Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar in...
East Central Custer County in southeastern Colorado...
West Central Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 845 PM MDT.

* At 547 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the North and Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Between
0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 2 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation
and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the North and Middle Aspen
Acres Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
North and Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah and San Isabel.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake, Northcreek Road county line to Red Mountain Camp
and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 5:34PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
At 534 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 27
miles northwest of Parachute, or 46 miles north of Grand Junction,
moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of south central Rio
Blanco County.
properties.areaDesc: Central Yampa River Basin; Roan and Tavaputs Plateaus

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 5:27PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 526 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from near Texas Creek to 14 miles southeast of
Cotopaxi. Movement was northeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph, hail up to penny size hail, and
torrential rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible. Heavy rainfall could cause ponding of water on
paved road surfaces, washouts on dirt roads, and quick
runoff causing high flows in area creeks, streams and
normally dry washouts.

Locations impacted include...
Royal Gorge and Canon City.
